text:
maria: CI perf alert — canary p95 for the gpu runtime jumped ~38% after yesterday's merge (commit abc1234). Deploy flagged as rollout-blocker. Anyone available? :warning:
ci-bot: PERF TEST FAILED: tests/perf/canary_latency_longseq — p95=210ms (threshold 150ms) — job: nightly/canary-gpu-rt — dashboard: https://perf.example.com/runs/17722
alex: taking this. starting a bisect on main now. will post findings.
sam: quick note: my local profile showed kernel selector switching to int8_fused path for sequences >512 after the merge. that path has worse mem-copy pattern for our attention layout. attaching flamegraph shortly.
lee: KV cache hit-rate in canary dropped too — from 0.87 -> 0.43 around the same time. looks correlated with batch boundaries shifting.
alex: git bisect narrowed it to commit 88f7d5c — changeset touched batching heuristics + kernel selector heuristics. creating a minimal repro.
maria: if bisect is clean and it's that commit, we should revert to get the rollout moving. agree?
alex: confirmed. minimal repro reproduces p95 spike. opening revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421 — roll back heuristics tweak.
ci-bot: REVERT PR CREATED: #3421 — CI triggered: perf-suite queued.
sam: posted pprof and diff: https://gist.github.com/sam/pprof-diff — shows extra memcpy and 2x stall in attention kernel when int8_fused is chosen for long sequence.
lee: after revert landed to staging, canary metrics returned to baseline (p95 ~148ms). KV cache hit-rate back to 0.86. staging looks clean.
maria: good. let's not just revert and move on — need a post-release retro and concrete actions to avoid regressions: tighter perf tests, kernel-selection unit test, kv-cache regression detector, and tweak thresholds.
alex: agreed. propose: (1) add targeted micro-bench for kernel selector with randomized seq-length distributions, (2) add kv-cache hit-rate assertion in perf tests, (3) add a canary smoke job that runs on every merge that touches heuristics.
sam: also we should record a small synthetic workload that reproduces this cache/batching interaction and include it in nightly perf harness. current perf test only used fixed batch sizes which missed the distribution shift.
maria: good call. also make thresholds stricter: p95 threshold to +/-15% over baseline for canary-gpu-rt tests instead of current +/-30%.
lee: FYI the perf flakiness root cause for one of the tests was non-deterministic RNG seeding in the harness. I already pushed a quick fix to seed the workload generator in CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-config/pull/78
alex: I'll add an automated bisect hook for perf failures that can optionally produce a revert PR draft. We should be careful with automation, but it cuts manual time.
maria: assign action items — alex: add micro-bench and bisect hook ticket (#5678). sam: add kernel-selection unit tests + synthetic workload (#5679). lee: add kv-cache assertion and tighten thresholds in perf config (#5680). ops: run a one-week watch on canary after we re-enable rollout.
sam: writing up a short retro doc with timeline, root cause (kernel-selector heuristic + batch-distribution change -> memcopy contention -> kv-cache fragmentation), and proposed fixes. will link it here when done.
ci-bot: PERF SUITE: after revert, nightly/canary-gpu-rt passes.
maria: thanks all — great triage. let's land the tests this week before re-enabling the rollouts that touch batching heuristics. :thumbsup:
lee: will open PR for perf config changes today.
alex: starting work on bisect-hook tomorrow.
sam: retro doc posted: https://docs.internal/redwood/perf/retro-1772201234 — includes flamegraphs and repro steps.
maria: perfect. closing thread once PRs are linked.
